text:
alex: Quick ask — can someone run a short throughput smoke for continuous batching tuning on staging? I want to validate small-window ramp behavior with two scenarios: steady and burst. Specs: max_batch=8, max_tokens=2048, queue_window=40ms. Need 2x ~2min runs: one steady at 64 rps, one with burst (64 -> 400 rps for 30s). cc @jordan @maria
maria: I can run one now. Which loadgen profile and payload set should I use?
jordan: Use the cb_small_window profile in loadgen. Command roughly: 
```
loadgen --profile cb_small_window --clients 8 --duration 120 --payloads synth_short.json --tags cb-sweep-2423456789
```
Also include warmup (--warmup 20) so KV cache isn't cold.
alex: perfect. add header X-Run-Tag:cb-sweep-2423 and enable tracing (trace=1) for first run.
dev-bot: test job queued: cb-sweep-2423456789 (id: job-8301)
sam: Heads up — gpu-node gpu-3 has flaky clocks during bursts, exclude it (label: avoid-gpu3).
maria: kicking off run1 (steady) on g4dn x4 without gpu-3; will post logs when done.
lee: quick question — do we want to compare quant variants in the same run or separate? t7q vs t7.
ajex: (typo) alex: separate runs please, easier to attribute. Run quant baseline first (t7), then t7q.
jordan: also recommend a second probe where max_batch=4 and queue_window=80ms to test lower batching with higher window. Might help tail under burst.
maria: first run done. Summary: steady 64rps, median latency 42ms, p95 210ms, p99 380ms. No errors. Uploading logs at: https://internal-logs/runs/job-8301
--- paste from runtime metrics ---
peak_rps: 68
avg_latency_ms: 51
p95_latency_ms: 210
error_rate: 0%
---
alex: solid. ok start burst run now with the burst pattern: 64rps steady, jump to 400rps for 30s at t=30s.
maria: starting burst run (will tag cb-burst-2423456789).
dev-bot: run started (job-8302)
maria: mid-run note — saw a short spike in queue length at burst start, queue_length peaked 1.2k reqs, runtime auto-fallback triggered to variant t7-lt for ~12s, requests succeeded.
ajex: (alex) thanks, can you attach which machines were serving during fallback?
maria: serving set: g4dn-01,g4dn-02,g4dn-04 (g4dn-03 excluded). Fallback window correlates with g4dn-02 GC spike.
sam: filing infra note to ops about g4dn-02. @lee can you watch that node?
lee: on it, will ssh and check after run finishes.
maria: burst run finished. Summary: peak 380rps sustained for ~28s, median latency 48ms, p95 260ms, p99 680ms during fallback spikes; overall error rate 0.6% (mostly timeouts at fallback boundary). Full traces and flamegraphs uploaded to: https://perf-traces/job-8302
jordan: interesting — fallback helped keep success rate >99% but tail worsened. For next experiment: reduce max_batch to 4 + queue_window 80ms (as suggested) and try another burst. Also try forcing no-fallback to measure fail mode.
alex: schedule the second variant run (max_batch=4, queue_window=80ms) tomorrow 09:30 PT, please coordinate with oncall. If p99 increases >10% vs baseline, mark as regression.
maria: scheduled, will include both quant variants and one forced-no-fallback run.
dev-bot: reminder queued: ops oncall ping at 09:25 PT
lee: checked g4dn-02 logs — collector shows a CPU steal during the window, probably infra noise. I'll cordon it for the next run.
alex: thanks team. After the scheduled runs, please paste a 3-line summary in this thread (peak rps, p95, p99) and attach the small perf diff table. If anything looks like regression (>10% tail increase), auto-rollout to t7-lt is allowed as short-term mitigation. :thumbsup:
